stem: Which one of the following features would be most concerning in a child with stridor?
explanation: Biphasic stridor is most concerning because it suggests fixed or more severe upper airway obstruction involving both inspiratory and expiratory phases, and may indicate a potentially serious lesion or worsening airway compromise.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Breathing difficulties

optionExplanations.A: Loud stridor can occur in upper airway obstruction but does not by itself indicate the most dangerous feature.
optionExplanations.B: Fever may suggest croup or infection, but fever alone is less concerning than biphasic stridor.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Biphasic stridor is a red flag for significant upper airway obstruction and warrants urgent assessment.
optionExplanations.D: Wheeze suggests lower airway obstruction rather than the upper airway process indicated by stridor.
optionExplanations.E: A history of allergy may be relevant to anaphylaxis, but it is not as concerning as biphasic stridor as a feature in the child described.

Clinical scenario 3 - Harry

Harry, a two year old boy, presents with a barking cough and stridor at rest. He had been well up until this evening, apart from a mild runny nose and slight cough. On examination he has moderate respiratory distress with intercostal and subcostal recessions and tug. His RR is 35, HR 140 and saturations 94% in room air. He has a clear chest and inspiratory stridor at rest. He has been previously well and his immunisations are up to date.

The following five questions refer to Harry's clinical scenario.
